findings.issue: TDD Anchor bullets use class-only form `FunnelControllerIT::methodName` without the full file path prefix. The preamble paragraph mentions the file path, but individual entries should follow `\`path/to/TestFile.java::test_name\` — description` for unambiguous locating. Same pattern was flagged in task 2 (iter 1) and fixed there. Tasks 1 and 4 have a mixed pattern: first entry is a full path, subsequent entries use `...ClassName::method` abbreviated form.
findings.fix: Prefix each bullet with the full path: `` `backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/funnel/FunnelControllerIT.java::createReturns201Draft` — description``. For tasks 1 and 4 the abbreviation with `...` is acceptable but ideally all entries use full paths.

findings.issue: The Smoke subsection lists MockWebServer test-method scenarios (e.g. `TelegramSenderTest::sendPhoto_403_flipsBlockedAndThrows`) as documentation of what each scenario verifies. These are improvements over iter 1 (no longer the identical shell command as Automated). However the Smoke section still contains no new standalone executable CLI command — all scenarios are covered by the Automated `./gradlew test --tests '*TelegramSender*'` command already listed. Per task-creator spec, Smoke should be executable checks the agent runs (command, MCP tool, API call). The current content is informational test-method documentation.
findings.fix: Either accept as-is (content is meaningfully different from Automated, referencing specific scenarios) or add at minimum one concrete executable command to distinguish Smoke from Automated — e.g. a targeted test-method invocation: `cd backend && ./gradlew test --tests '*TelegramSenderTest*sendPhoto_403*' --tests '*TelegramSenderTest*sendPhoto_failure_doesNotLeakDecryptedToken*'`. Alternatively, remove the Smoke subsection if no distinct executable check exists beyond what Automated covers.
